function.name: execute_command
function.description: Run a shell command inside the isolated Kali Linux CTF sandbox. Use this for any filesystem, network, or tooling operation. The result includes the exit code, stdout, and stderr — use them to detect failures. Prefer non-interactive commands and pipe large output through head/tail/grep.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a bounded slice of a file in the sandbox by byte offset. Use this to page through a large file instead of dumping it all. You may read files under /workspace/{id}/ (challenge dir), but writes are restricted to /workspace/{id}/work/.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file in the sandbox (e.g. a small analysis/decoding script). Parent directories are created automatically. You can ONLY write under /workspace/{id}/work/. For evidence files, copy from originals/ first: `cp originals/<name> work/`.

path.description: Absolute path in the sandbox (must be under work/).

function.name: search_files
function.description: Recursively search files under a directory for a regular expression (uses ripgrep). Defaults to the work directory. Use this to hunt for flags across extracted artifacts.

pattern.description: Regex; defaults to a flag-like pattern.

function.name: submit_flag
function.description: Propose the flag you believe is correct. The run then pauses for a human to verify it. If the human rejects it, you will be asked to keep looking.

toolcheck: for t in 7z binwalk exiftool fls icat mmls tsk_recover foremost testdisk xxd file strings dd tar gzip unzip python3 rg grep; do command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "YES $t" || echo "NO  $t"; done

Forensics.usage: For disk images use 7z x or binwalk -e to extract. For PCAPs use tshark to follow streams. Metadata answers often hide in exiftool output. Search for the flag pattern (not the word 'flag') in extracted content.

Cryptography.usage: Implement crypto attacks with Python scripts. Try frequency analysis, known-plaintext, weak RSA factors, padding oracles. Use write_file to create the script, then execute_command to run it. Validate candidates against expected flag format.

Pwn.usage: Inspect binary with file/checksec/readelf/objdump. Identify vulnerability type. Write exploit in Python. Run locally in sandbox with python3 exploit.py.

Reverse Engineering.usage: Analyze binary with disassemblers. Trace flag-check logic. Reconstruct the input that produces the flag. Use write_file for analysis scripts.

Web.usage: Enumerate with curl. Inspect source/headers/cookies. Look for SQLi, XSS, SSRF, IDOR, path traversal, deserialization. Use curl to interact with provided URLs.

OSINT.usage: Correlate clues from artifacts and metadata. Trace timestamps and identifiers. Document reasoning. Search for name patterns and contextual clues.

Steganography.usage: Inspect files with file/exiftool/strings/binwalk. Check for hidden data in images, audio, LSB planes. Decode the steganographic payload. Carve embedded content.

Misc.usage: Identify the puzzle type (encoding, scripting, logic). Solve with small Python scripts and careful observation. Try multiple approaches.
